lines: BUTTERFLY FOREST. A public garden of the county council. Open from sunrise to sunset.
Do not pick the flowers. Visitors are counted in at the gate and counted out again.

Under it, the plan of the gardens as they were. THE LAWN is inside THE GATE, and THE KEEPER'S HUT past it. THE RIDES go round the hut, and off them THE HEARTH, THE ROCKERY, THE MAZE, THE WATER GARDEN and THE STANDING STONE.
THE ROSE WALK is across THE WATER GARDEN, and THE GROTTO through THE MAZE. Butterflies are released at THE STANDING STONE, five at a time. Nets from THE KEEPER'S HUT.
Below, on a newer board in a different hand: the paths have grown over. Keep to the light.
Eleven cases on the wall, each with a label in the same careful hand. The labels are trades and not species. CARTER. NURSE. SIGNALMAN.
Ten of them have something in them.
The eleventh label is blank. The case is open, and there is a pin in it with nothing on the pin.
The case labelled NIGHT WATCHMAN has no wings in it. Pinned through the hole of a brass tally stamped G.M.Co. there is a key, and you take it.
The eleventh label is blank. The case is open, and there is a pin in it with nothing on the pin. The case labelled NIGHT WATCHMAN is empty now.
Eight of yours, set in the order the labels were written. The blank one is the one that fits them.
A charcoal burner's hearth, swept out, with the kettle still hung over it and next week's wood stacked.
The hedge is thick on three sides and there is one way in. You can sleep here.
It sits on your sleeve. You have nothing to keep it in, and it seems to know.

Bigger than your hand, and it does not mind the lamp. Nothing out here minds the lamp.
A butterfly over the road by the forest gate. Its colours are the ones that floated past the window in the tunnel.
It keeps a little way ahead of you, and then goes back toward the gate, as if it had been told how far to come.
THE GATE. Visitors are counted out here.
THE LAWN. The beds are planted where the sun comes down.
THE KEEPER'S HUT. Nets are issued here.
THE RIDES. Every garden opens off the rides.
THE HEARTH. A charcoal burner's. Visitors may rest by it.
THE ROCKERY. Mind the loose stone.
THE MAZE. Visitors are asked not to cut through the hedges.
THE WATER GARDEN. The footbridge is closed for repair.
THE STANDING STONE. Butterflies are released here, five at a time.
The path up to it has gone to bare earth.
